description: Hijackers crashed passenger planes into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon, killing nearly 3,000 people; a fourth plane crashed in Pennsylvania.
The United States and Britain began air strikes on Taliban and al-Qaeda targets in Afghanistan.
The energy company Enron filed for bankruptcy after disclosures of accounting fraud, the largest corporate bankruptcy in U.S. history at the time.
In his State of the Union address, President Bush called Iran, Iraq and North Korea an 'axis of evil'.
President Bush proposed a new cabinet-level Department of Homeland Security combining parts of more than 20 agencies.
The telecom company WorldCom disclosed that it had improperly booked nearly $4 billion of expenses.
Congress passed a resolution authorizing President Bush to use military force against Iraq.
Republicans gained seats in both chambers in the midterm elections and won control of the Senate.
The Space Shuttle Columbia broke apart during re-entry over Texas, killing all seven astronauts.
Secretary of State Colin Powell presented the administration's case to the UN Security Council that Iraq had weapons of mass destruction.
U.S.-led forces invaded Iraq after an ultimatum to Saddam Hussein expired.
U.S. forces took control of Baghdad, and a statue of Saddam Hussein was pulled down in Firdos Square.
Aboard an aircraft carrier under a 'Mission Accomplished' banner, President Bush announced the end of major combat operations in Iraq.
The U.S. announced that its forces had captured former Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein near Tikrit.
Photographs of U.S. soldiers abusing Iraqi detainees at Abu Ghraib prison were broadcast on television.
President Bush won re-election over John Kerry, and Republicans gained seats in the House and Senate.
President Bush signed a law passed by Congress to move the Terri Schiavo feeding-tube case to federal court.
Hurricane Katrina struck the Gulf Coast; levee failures flooded most of New Orleans, and thousands waited days for rescue and supplies.
President Bush nominated White House counsel Harriet Miers to the Supreme Court.
Scooter Libby, Vice President Cheney's chief of staff, was indicted for perjury and obstruction of justice in the CIA leak investigation.
It was disclosed that Vice President Cheney had accidentally shot a companion during a quail hunt in Texas.
President Bush threatened to veto any bill blocking a deal letting a Dubai state-owned company run operations at six major U.S. ports.
The U.S. announced that an airstrike had killed Abu Musab al-Zarqawi, the leader of al-Qaeda in Iraq.
Republican Congressman Mark Foley resigned after sexually explicit messages he sent to teenage congressional pages became public.
Democrats won control of the House and the Senate in the midterm elections; Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld resigned the next day.
President Bush announced that more than 20,000 additional U.S. troops would be sent to Iraq.
Reports described neglect and poor living conditions for wounded soldiers at Walter Reed Army Medical Center.
A gunman killed 32 people at Virginia Tech, then the deadliest shooting by a single gunman in U.S. history.
President Bush commuted Scooter Libby's 30-month prison sentence.
The investment bank Bear Stearns collapsed and was sold to JPMorgan Chase in a deal backed by the Federal Reserve.

President Obama signed the $787 billion American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, passed with almost no Republican votes.
President Obama nominated appeals judge Sonia Sotomayor to the Supreme Court.
General Motors filed for bankruptcy in a government-led restructuring that left the federal government its majority owner.
At a news conference, President Obama said Cambridge police 'acted stupidly' in arresting Harvard professor Henry Louis Gates at his home.
President Obama addressed a joint session of Congress on health care reform; Representative Joe Wilson shouted 'You lie!' during the speech.
President Obama was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize less than nine months into his presidency.
An Army psychiatrist killed 13 people in a shooting at Fort Hood, Texas.
President Obama announced that 30,000 more U.S. troops would go to Afghanistan, with withdrawals to begin in 2011.
A man tried to detonate explosives hidden in his underwear on a flight to Detroit before passengers subdued him.
Republican Scott Brown won the Massachusetts Senate special election for Ted Kennedy's former seat, ending the Democrats' 60-seat majority.
The House passed the Affordable Care Act 219-212 with no Republican votes; President Obama signed it two days later.
The Deepwater Horizon oil rig exploded in the Gulf of Mexico, killing 11 workers and starting the largest marine oil spill in U.S. history.
Republicans gained 63 House seats and took control of the House in the midterm elections.
A gunman shot Representative Gabrielle Giffords and 18 others at a constituent event in Tucson, killing six.
President Obama announced that U.S. special forces had killed Osama bin Laden in Pakistan.
After weeks of standoff, Congress raised the debt ceiling hours before a possible default; three days later S&P downgraded the U.S. credit rating for the first time.
Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi was killed by rebel fighters after a NATO-backed campaign.
President Obama spoke about the killing of Trayvon Martin, an unarmed Black teenager shot in Florida by a man who had not been charged.

description: Hurricane Sandy struck the Northeast, killing dozens and flooding parts of New York and New Jersey; President Obama and New Jersey Governor Chris Christie toured the damage together.
A gunman killed 20 children and six staff members at Sandy Hook Elementary School in Newtown, Connecticut.
Congress passed a last-minute deal averting the 'fiscal cliff', raising taxes on high earners and delaying automatic spending cuts.
Two bombs exploded near the finish line of the Boston Marathon, killing three people and injuring hundreds.
The IRS acknowledged that it had singled out conservative groups applying for tax-exempt status for extra scrutiny.
Leaked documents revealed that the National Security Agency was collecting the phone records of millions of Americans.
A Florida jury acquitted George Zimmerman in the killing of Trayvon Martin.
After a chemical weapons attack near Damascus, President Obama said he would ask Congress to authorize military strikes on Syria.
The federal government shut down for 16 days over Republican demands to defund the Affordable Care Act; the same day, the HealthCare.gov website launched with widespread technical failures.

Millions of people received cancellation notices for individual health plans that did not meet the Affordable Care Act's standards, despite the president's earlier promise that people could keep their plans.
Russia formally annexed Crimea after seizing the peninsula from Ukraine and holding a disputed referendum.
Veterans Affairs Secretary Eric Shinseki resigned after reports that VA hospitals kept secret waiting lists and veterans died waiting for care.
The U.S. freed five Taliban detainees held at Guantanamo in exchange for Army Sergeant Bowe Bergdahl, held captive in Afghanistan for five years.
A police officer shot and killed Michael Brown, an unarmed Black 18-year-old, in Ferguson, Missouri, followed by protests and a heavily armed police response.
ISIS released a video showing the beheading of the American journalist James Foley.
The first case of Ebola diagnosed in the United States was confirmed in Dallas.
Republicans won control of the Senate and expanded their House majority in the midterm elections.
President Obama announced executive actions shielding about four million undocumented immigrants from deportation.
Protests over the death of Freddie Gray in police custody turned into riots in Baltimore, and the governor declared a state of emergency.
A white supremacist killed nine Black worshippers at Emanuel AME Church in Charleston, South Carolina.
The Supreme Court ruled that same-sex couples have a constitutional right to marry, a day after upholding Affordable Care Act subsidies.
The U.S. and five other world powers reached a deal with Iran limiting its nuclear program in exchange for sanctions relief.
Coordinated ISIS attacks in Paris killed 130 people.
A married couple inspired by ISIS killed 14 people at a holiday party in San Bernardino, California.
Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia died; Senate Republican leaders said they would not consider any nominee until after the election.
President Obama nominated Judge Merrick Garland to the Supreme Court.
